accepted.text: The loop's preflight fails unless `permissions.allow` names each relay script at the exact path `<project.repo>/.claude/scripts/<script>`. A benchmark clone has a new repo path per `--out`, so every `prepare` needs new allow rules, and permission settings are human-only (invariant 6, so `prepare` must not write them). Spike F2 did not settle whether a mid-path wildcard (`.../bench/*/clone/...`) works in auto mode: the docs allow a `*` anywhere in a Bash rule, but on entering auto mode they drop "some wildcarded paths, like Bash($HOME/bin/*)", and do not say whether a mid-path `*` is one of them. Separately, the loop's own permission.js counts a rule only when the text before its first `*` names the script, so a mid-path wildcard fails the loop's check whatever Claude Code does. Both facts point the same way: use rules with the full literal script path and a trailing `*` only (narrow rules stay in effect in auto mode). Questions for the human: (a) accept a fixed `--out` (one set of rules, added once as H7, covers every run, and `prepare` refuses a different path), or add rules per run? (b) never use `mergePermission: "prompt"` in the bench base config, since auto mode refused the merges in Warden wave 4 and that would make the merge step differ from real use. Recommendation: (a) fixed `--out`, (b) never. `prepare` prints the exact rules but writes no settings. The mid-path question stays open (F2) but the recommendation does not depend on its answer.

accepted.text: The benchmark's only barrier against talking to real GitHub is that `gh` resolves to bench/bin/gh through a prepended PATH. F1 did not show whether BENCH_STATE and BENCH_CI_JOBS, or a PATH set at launch, reach Bash calls and Workflow relays; it only shows that an `export` inside one Bash command does not carry to the next. Local probe (read-only, run 2026-11-26): ~/.zprofile and ~/.zshrc prepend several directories to PATH (Python framework bins, nvm, solana, ~/dev/reps/bin, ~/.local/bin, /opt/anaconda3/bin, ~/.cargo/bin). /etc/zprofile runs path_helper. None of these startup files sets gh or a gh shim. `which -a gh` in this shell returns one result, /usr/local/bin/gh, so no prepended directory shadows the real gh here. BENCH_STATE and BENCH_CI_JOBS are not set in this shell, so the probe could not show whether they survive. The probe ran in a plain shell, not in a Workflow subagent relay or a Claude Code Bash tool call, so it does not show what those contexts see.

Docs (code.claude.com Tools reference, published 2026-11-25): Claude Code starts a non-interactive shell, sources ~/.zshrc for Zsh, and applies the aliases, functions and shell options it captures to Bash commands. Environment variables do not persist between Bash commands: an export in one command is not available in the next. The docs say to activate a virtualenv or conda environment before launching Claude Code, which suggests the launching shell's environment is inherited, but the docs do not state that explicitly. The docs say nothing about Workflow subagent relays. Consequence for the question: ~/.zshrc PATH lines do apply to Bash tool calls, and a variable set only by an export in one command will not carry to the next.

Not settled: whether BENCH_STATE and BENCH_CI_JOBS, or a PATH set in the launching shell, reach every Bash tool call and every Workflow subagent relay unchanged. That needs a live probe from inside a Claude Code session and a relay, e.g. `echo $BENCH_STATE $BENCH_CI_JOBS; command -v gh` run in a Bash tool call and in a relay, with the variables exported before launch.

spikes.fact: Does Claude Code's permission system, and auto mode in particular, accept a `permissions.allow` rule with a wildcard in the middle of the path, such as `Bash(node /x/*/clone/.claude/scripts/merge-pr.js *)`, as an allow rule without asking the classifier? The loop's permission.js counts a rule only when the text before its first `*` names the script.
spikes.answer: Partly settled. The docs confirm that a * in a Bash allow rule can sit in the middle, and that a matching allow rule resolves immediately without the classifier in auto mode, with exceptions. They do not settle whether a mid-path wildcard in a path survives auto mode. Confirmed: (1) "A * in a Bash rule matches any text, including spaces" and "A * can go anywhere in the rule: at the start, in the middle, or at the end" (examples: Bash(git log * main), Bash(git * main)). (2) "Claude Code matches everything before the first * as written", so the words before the first * are what limit the rule. (3) In auto mode, "Actions matching your allow, ask, or deny rules resolve immediately, with these exceptions" (protected paths, critical-path rm/rmdir, requiresUserInteraction MCP tools, commands with per-command allowed domains, Claude in Chrome actions, ask rules on command content, network-path reads). Everything else goes to the classifier. (4) On entering auto mode, these allow rules are DROPPED: blanket Bash(*), wildcarded interpreters like Bash(python*), a wrapper followed only by a wildcard like Bash(timeout *), shell rules starting with a wildcard like Bash(* --version), "Some wildcarded paths, like Bash($HOME/bin/*) or PowerShell(C:\tools\x.exe *)", package-manager run commands, Agent allow rules, and Monitor allow rules. Narrow rules like Bash(npm test) stay in effect. The docs do not say whether Bash(node /x/*/clone/... *) falls under the "wildcarded paths" drop; the examples given are trailing wildcards. The docs do not state that the classifier overrides allow rules in general. Not settled from the docs: how the loop's permission.js prefix check relates to Claude Code's own matching, and whether a mid-path wildcard in a path is treated as a wildcarded path for the auto-mode drop.

spikes.fact: How much weekly Claude Code usage is left on the account, and is it enough for about 1.7M tokens per replay of wave 1 times the planned runs (about 10M for two configs at 3 runs) beside the other sessions on it?
spikes.answer: Not settled from any source. Anthropic publishes no token or hour figures for Claude Code weekly limits, so the 10M-token budget cannot be checked against a published cap. The remaining balance on this account is not visible from documentation. It can only be read in the account itself with /usage in Claude Code (or the usage settings page on claude.ai), and I did not run that because it is an account read, not a documentation fact. What the official source does say: the 5-hour session limit is separate from the weekly limit; a temporary 50% weekly boost ran May 13 to September 13, 2026; from September 14, 2026 eligible plans' weekly limits are 25% higher than before the promotion. The official page does not describe a shared pool between Claude Code and other sessions. A third-party guide says Claude Code, Claude chat and Cowork share one pool, but that is unverified, so whether the other sessions draw from the same weekly limit is also unsettled. Third-party sources give Max 5x and 20x as multiples of Pro per 5-hour session, and they disagree on the weekly reset mechanics.
